name: Mind Mapping
description:
Mind mapping is a visual technique for expanding and organising ideas around a central topic. Related concepts branch outward from a central node, allowing associations, subtopics and relationships to become visible on a single surface.

It can support individual thinking or collaborative exploration and is particularly useful before the structure of a problem is fully understood.
whenToUse: Use mind mapping when exploring the scope of a topic, organising early research questions or generating associations around a design challenge.
steps: Write the central topic or question in the middle.
Add major related ideas as branches.
Extend each branch with more specific concepts.
Add connections between branches where relationships emerge.
Continue until significant areas and gaps become visible.
Review the map for clusters, contradictions and missing perspectives.
Reorganise it if a clearer structure emerges.
Use the map to identify research questions or areas for further development.
lookOutFor: A mind map records associations, not necessarily evidence.
The structure can reflect the assumptions of the person who created it.
Avoid treating the first hierarchy that emerges as the definitive structure of the problem.

resources.citation: Buzan, T. & Buzan, B. (1993). *The Mind Map Book*. BBC Books.
